Scrape book reviews from Goodreads using RSelenium

Source: R/scrape_reviews.R
scrape_reviews.Rd

This function scrapes book reviews from Goodreads based on provided book IDs using RSelenium for dynamic content loading to retrieve more than 30 reviews.

Usage

scrape_reviews(
  book_ids_path,
  num_reviews = 30,
  use_parallel = FALSE,
  num_cores = 4,
  delay_min = 2,
  delay_max = 5,
  browser_type = "firefox",
  headless = TRUE
)

Arguments

book_ids_path

A character string specifying the path to a file containing book IDs.

num_reviews

An integer specifying the number of reviews to scrape per book. Default is 30.

use_parallel

A logical value indicating whether to use parallel processing. Default is FALSE.

num_cores

An integer specifying the number of cores to use for parallel processing. Default is 4.

delay_min

Minimum delay between requests in seconds. Default is 2.

delay_max

Maximum delay between requests in seconds. Default is 5.

browser_type

Browser type for RSelenium ("firefox", "chrome", "phantomjs"). Default is "firefox".

headless

Whether to run browser in headless mode. Default is TRUE.

Value

A data frame containing scraped review information.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Create a temporary file with sample book IDs
temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines(c("1420", "2767052", "10210"), temp_file)
# Run the function (with a small number of reviews to keep the example quick)
reviews <- scrape_reviews(temp_file, num_reviews = 50, use_parallel = FALSE)
